verdict: NOT CONSISTENT — do not freeze. FR numbering is clean (FR-1..FR-236, every ID defined exactly once, every section inside its allocated range, no gaps, no duplicates) and every one of SI-1..SI-12 is upheld and named by at least one FR, so there are no orphaned safety invariants. But the draft carries ~20 live contradictions, of which six are hard numeric/mechanism conflicts that two sections would implement differently (outbound queue bound 20,000 vs 5,000; alert-history retention; Driver kill-switch mechanism; ATS posture vs the gate that forbids it; user-imported alert sounds vs bundled-only; the Watch preference set and its "theme" control). Of the six disagreements the research pre-flagged, only two are genuinely settled (required-check *naming*, and the deployment floor — the latter settled in §6 but still reproduced as open in 5.12 and §15). Keychain class is settled in every FR yet §15 still lists it blocking. Reconnect policy, wrist alert transport and the glucose validation window are reproduced verbatim, the last of them inside a single section (FR-138 vs FR-153). The most serious structural finding is not an orphaned invariant but the inverse: SI-1's "no device command anywhere" is contradicted by FR-30/FR-31/FR-234's calibration Capability, and FR-205's own gate would fail the shipping protocol if `calibrate` is declared — that needs a ruling before any Driver protocol is written. Three verified Tandem safety behaviours (sensor-validity status byte, IOB selector byte, trend-arrow provenance) are covered by no FR and no Parity Ledger row; §15 records them as unowned, which is an acknowledgement, not a requirement. Vocabulary discipline is good in 5.1/5.2/5.7/5.10/5.11 and materially weaker in 5.8 and 5.9, which use "server URL" and "cloud-source" as normative terms where the Glossary says Backend.

contradictions: OUTBOUND QUEUE BOUND — 20,000 vs 5,000. FR-142 (5.8-data-sync.md:112), PD-23 (7-parity-ledger.md:160) and A-31 all fix the bound at 20,000 rows and explain why Android's 5,000 would discard Pump history overnight. NFR-7's data-volume table (6-nfrs.md:187) and NFR-16 (6-nfrs.md:355) both state 'the outbound queue caps at 5000 rows and prunes oldest-first'. Two sections give the enforced cap a different number, and §6 opens by saying it will not restate numbers other sections own.

ALERT-HISTORY RETENTION — FR-87 re-ships the defect FR-139 closes. FR-87 (5.4-alerting.md:296): 'Alerts older than 7 days are pruned when the history screen opens.' FR-139 (5.8) makes the alert history follow the user's 1–30 day retention window and run on every execution opportunity, and PD-19 explicitly names 'retention pinned at a fixed 7 days, and cleanup running only when the alerts screen is opened' as the Android defect being corrected. FR-87 states the uncorrected version as a requirement.

DRIVER KILL SWITCH — runtime flag vs compilation condition. FR-27 (5.2): 'The gate is a build setting read at runtime, not a compile-time conditional: gated code stays compiled and stays covered by tests.' FR-189 (5.10): 'Disabling it is a compilation condition, not a runtime flag: the Driver module is absent from the binary… strictly stronger than Android's runtime kill switch, which left the plugin present but inert.' PD-11 sides with FR-189. These are opposite mechanisms with opposite consequences for test coverage and for FR-22's 'the list doubles as what does this build contain'.

ATS POSTURE — the settled Info.plist would fail the PRD's own gate. 5.9's description (lines 20-22) records it as settled: 'blanket cleartext allowed at the platform layer, with the app's private-address-only policy as the sole guard', and PL-50 restates that as the substitute ('Blanket cleartext at the platform layer with no local-networking key'). FR-204 (5.11): 'ATS: any `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`… fails the gate.' NFR-20: 'a Required Check fails any pull request that adds or widens an ATS exception'. §15 OQ-45 still asks the question the 5.9 note claims is settled.

DEBUG-BUILD CLEARTEXT — FR-163 (5.9) widens the rule FR-150 fixes. FR-163: 'https is always allowed; http is allowed only in a debug build, OR when the opt-in is on AND the host classifies as private.' FR-150 (5.8) and NFR-20: http is permitted only on the conjunction (private host AND explicit opt-in), enforced at save time and again per request. FR-163's disjunction permits cleartext to ANY host in a debug configuration — and §15 OQ-48 already establishes that a Builder can install a debug configuration through their own TestFlight.

ALERT SOUNDS — user-imported vs bundled-only. FR-67 (5.4): 'User-imported sounds are transcoded to ≤ 30 s CAF and written into the app container's `Library/Sounds/`; a file exceeding 30 s is rejected at import.' FR-170 (5.9): 'Sounds are files shipped inside the app bundle or its container… No arbitrary system ringtone or user content URI is selectable.' PL-29 records the substitute as 'A curated bundled set' with user-visible impact 'The user cannot pick their own ringtone'. FR-67 requires an import path the other two say does not exist.

ALARM VOLUME CONTROL — FR-170 offers a control FR-66 and PL-24 forbid. FR-66 (5.4): 'No code attempts to set output, ringer or alarm volume, and no code reads or infers the silent-switch position.' PL-24: 'Deleted, not ported. No code sets, reads or infers volume or switch position.' FR-170 (5.9): 'A volume control for low alerts is present, and its copy states plainly what iOS actually guarantees…' PL-23 then cites 'FR-170 volume-control copy' as a disclosure surface for a control that cannot exist.

WATCH PREFERENCE SET — FR-134 and FR-172 disagree on both names and contents. FR-134 (5.7) offers Show IOB, Show Glucose Graph, Wrist Alerts, Graph Range and four overlays, and states: 'No preference is offered that nothing consumes — in particular no watch-face theme and no show seconds control', rebinding 'theme' to a Watch-app-only high-contrast preference (A-28). FR-172 (5.9) offers 'Alert Vibration' (not Wrist Alerts) and 'theme (Dark, Clinical Blue, High Contrast)' — the exact Android face theme PL-33 records as a forced loss.

NEGATIVE-AGE FRESHNESS — one shared function, two rules. FR-49 (5.3): 'A negative age (clock skew, future-dated timestamp) classifies as Fresh for display only', and 'The classifier, its thresholds and the relative-age label live in a module that BOTH the app and the Watch app link, so no second definition can exist (SI-4).' FR-123 (5.7): 'An age more negative than -60,000 ms fails closed on both axes: the Freshness Tier resolves to Too Stale', pinned by FR-116 as a shared-module unit test ('age -60,000 ms Fresh / -60,001 ms Too Stale'). At age −120 s the same linked function must return Fresh on the phone and Too Stale on the wrist.

GLUCOSE VALIDATION WINDOW (research contradiction 8 — REPRODUCED, and inside one section). FR-32 (5.2) requires every Driver to validate against the CURRENT, Backend-narrowable Safety Limits at every validation pass. FR-138 (5.8) says rejection against 'the CURRENT bounds' applies 'at every entry point: reading construction, cloud ingestion, history extraction and read-back from the store'. FR-153 (5.8), five FRs later, validates Nightscout-sourced rows against the ABSOLUTE 20–500 Glucose Validity Bound. §15 OQ-4 still lists this blocking. The consequence the research named — a narrowed Safety Limit silently changing Time in Range, GMI, CV and the Alert Floor's input set for one source but not the other — is stated nowhere in §5.

CALIBRATION vs SI-1 (research contradiction 1 — REPRODUCED, highest severity). SI-1 forbids any 'device command' in any Driver protocol. FR-30 keeps 'calibration target' in the closed seven-Capability set; FR-31 says 'Connect, disconnect, calibrate, unpair and reconnect are the only device-touching operations and are classified as session and lifecycle, not therapy'; FR-234 publishes 'CGM calibration, Bluetooth pair and unpair, and connect and disconnect' as permitted non-therapeutic operations. FR-205 then fails CI on 'any therapeutic write primitive — bolus, basal, pump-setting, or any device command' added to any Capability protocol. If `calibrate` is declared, the shipping Driver protocol trips the project's own snapshot gate; if it is not, FR-30's Capability is vestigial and FR-234 publishes a capability that does not exist. §15 OQ-6 flags it blocking; nothing in §5 resolves it.

WRIST ALERT TRANSPORT (research contradiction 9 — REPRODUCED). FR-128/FR-129 (5.7) mandate a notification scheduled ON the Watch, 'triggered by a guaranteed delivery from the app that wakes the Watch app in the background even when suspended', plus a Watch-local 30-minute re-alarm ladder. FR-67 and FR-77 (5.4) are written against iPhone mirroring ('Acknowledging the mirrored notification on Apple Watch routes the action back to the iPhone app'; 'a notification mirrored onto Apple Watch plays watchOS's own alert sound'). PL-30 asserts both in one cell: 'System mirroring is treated as the only wrist buzz path by design; wrist alerts are Watch-scheduled…'. §15 OQ-3 still lists it blocking. Compounding: two re-alarm ladders now coexist with different cadences — FR-76's phone-side 5 repeats at 120 s ending at 10 minutes, and FR-129's Watch-side 30-minute ladder — with no FR reconciling what the user experiences.

RECONNECT POLICY (research contradiction 4 — PARTIALLY REPRODUCED). FR-13: 'No attempt cap, no maximum-failures abort… unless the user unpaired, the app keeps trying', and 'A named review rule forbids attempt caps, give-up conditions and app-scheduled reconnect timers in the connection layer.' FR-6: 'The secure handshake is bounded at 30 s; expiry latches Auth Failed, stops advertising and disables auto-reconnect.' FR-8: 'Auth Failed is latched and terminal for auto-reconnect.' FR-13 picks the foreground-ladder-plus-indefinite-pending-connect option, but its absolute 'no give-up condition' is contradicted by the Auth-Failed latch two FRs earlier, and §15 OQ-2 still lists the whole question blocking.

REQUIRED-CHECK ROSTER (research contradiction 5 — name resolved, roster not). FR-197 fixes the roster at exactly five job names and separately enumerates the seven non-required jobs. But FR-21, FR-31, FR-177, FR-179, FR-182, FR-189, FR-190, FR-194, FR-204, FR-205, FR-211, FR-214, FR-217, FR-219, NFR-1 and NFR-4 each assert that 'a Required Check' fails on their condition, and none of those checks appears in either list. §10 folds only FR-204's Entitlements and Plist Guard into `Static Analysis Gate`; the Driver Catalog check, the Driver API snapshot gate, the License Header Gate, the Contract Pin guards, the Safety Constant drift guard, the docs publication gate, the identifier registry check and the deployment-floor check are unmapped. 5.9's own note and §15 OQ-8 flag one instance as unowned; the class is larger than one.

KEYCHAIN ACCESSIBILITY CLASS (research contradiction 2 — RESOLVED in §5, REPRODUCED in §15). Every FR that touches it agrees on device-only after-first-unlock (FR-14, FR-18, FR-29, FR-75, FR-136, FR-161, FR-169, FR-181, NFR-18), and FR-204 makes any other class a build failure by name (`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`). Yet §15 OQ-1 still lists it '(blocking)' and unresolved, describing a Medtronic recommendation that no FR carries. Either §15 is stale or FR-204 is asserting a decision that was not made.

DEPLOYMENT FLOOR (research contradiction 12 — RESOLVED in §6, REPRODUCED in 5.12 and §15). NFR-1 fixes iOS 17.0 / watchOS 10.0, reconciles the two research figures, and requires the floor to appear once as a build setting read by the docs generator. FR-223's A-45 still carries both figures ('the evidence carries both that and an iOS 18 / watchOS 11 figure') as an open assumption; 5.12's Open Questions and §15 OQ-5 both still ask ('If §6 did not fix it, it must be fixed here'). §6's own note instructs 5.12 to be updated; it was not.

PHONE CHART Y-AXIS vs THE 'ONE CLAMP' RULE. FR-52 (5.3) fixes the Home/detail chart at 40–300 mg/dL with out-of-axis readings pinned to the boundary. FR-133 (5.7) declares 'One Y-axis clamp is used by every graph surface — the wrist sparkline, the full-screen Watch graph, and the iPhone widgets' spanning 20–500, and justifies it with 'No reading inside the Glucose Validity Bound is visible on one chart and clipped off another.' PD-16 claims that defect is closed. It is not: a 35 mg/dL reading renders truthfully on the wrist and pinned on the phone.

BACKEND-OPTIONAL NETWORK SILENCE. NFR-23: 'In Backend-optional mode the app makes **no** network requests at all', and 'The app makes no network request to any host other than the Backend the user configured… A test asserts the outbound host set.' FR-173 and FR-188 require an upstream release check over https to `github.com` and `objects.githubusercontent.com`, and FR-236 enumerates it as outbound connection (5). Nothing gates that check on Backend configuration, so NFR-23's asserted host-set test would fail against FR-188.

WATCH APP INSTALL PATH. FR-115: 'Installing or updating the app installs or updates the Watch app; there is no second downloadable artifact', and its mismatch banner links 'to the system Watch app's install flow'. FR-224 restates the no-separate-install rule. FR-172 (5.9) renders a hint card for 'not-installed with instructions to install it from TestFlight', and FR-173 directs a version mismatch to 'update the app from TestFlight'. Three different remedies for one condition, one of which (install the Watch app from TestFlight) contradicts the single-bundle model.

CUSTOM URL SCHEME vs DEEP LINKS. NFR-22: 'The app registers no custom URL scheme that accepts data from another app'. FR-63, FR-105 and FR-114 all require deep links to resolve — FR-114 specifically requires 'A prefill carried by an entry point is truncated to 500 characters', i.e. a deep link that accepts data. Research confirms Android registers no deep links at all, so this is additive scope; it has no PA row either.
gaps: TANDEM SENSOR-VALIDITY GATE (`egvStatusId`) — no FR, no Parity Ledger row. Verified in the research at `StatusResponseParser.kt:198-202`: `val egvStatus = cargo[6].toInt() and 0xFF; if (egvStatus !in 1..3) return null` (0=INVALID, 2=LOW, 3=HIGH, 4=UNAVAILABLE), with five dedicated test cases. This is the sensor's own claim that the value is usable and is entirely independent of the 20–500 Glucose Validity Bound. Nothing in 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 or 5.4 requires it, and no PL/PD row records its absence. A port that keeps the range check and drops this one renders warm-up and error sentinels as real, in-range, alertable glucose. §15 OQ-7(a) names it as unowned — that is an acknowledgement, not a requirement, and it belongs in the same enforcement tier as the Bound (arguably in the Safety Invariant Register).

TANDEM IOB SELECTOR BYTE (`iobType`) — no FR, no Parity Ledger row. The ControlIQIOBResponse 17-byte cargo carries BOTH a Mudaliar IOB and a Swan-6hr IOB, with a trailing selector byte choosing the live one (0 = Control-IQ off, 1 = on). FR-46 and FR-121 require 'IOB is displayed exactly as reported by the Pump' and 'IOB is the value the Pump reported' without saying which of the two the Pump reported. Both values are inside every bound the PRD enforces, so picking wrong produces a plausible, wrong, dosing-relevant number that no check catches. §15 OQ-7(b) only.

TREND-ARROW PROVENANCE — no FR, no Parity Ledger row. `cgmTrendIconId` comes from HomeScreenMirror opcode 56/57, not from the EGV response, so the trend glyph and the glucose value are separate transactions that can disagree and can age independently. FR-46 renders them 'both in the same colour' at one Freshness Tier; FR-120 renders `120 ->` as a single unit. On iOS the two reads can land in different background wakes, which makes the coupling assumption strictly worse than on Android. §15 OQ-7(c) only.

ANALYTICS SETTINGS AS A BACKEND-SYNCED OBJECT — the day-boundary hour is covered (FR-57, FR-89) but the Backend-synced BOLUS-CATEGORY LABEL OVERRIDE MAP is owned by nobody. FR-40 reconciles 'analytics config' and FR-167 clears 'analytics settings' on sign-out, but no FR defines what they are. FR-89 and FR-91 route category labels exclusively through the Driver's bolus-category-provider Capability; the Android `AnalyticsSettingsStore` label map from the Backend has no FR and no ledger row (research coverage gap 9).

APP GROUP / TARGET-TOPOLOGY DATA CONTRACT — unscoped. FR-181 templates the App Group container on the Builder's Team ID and FR-116 has the widget extension 'read the shared on-device cache directly', but no FR states which targets exist, what crosses the App Group boundary versus WatchConnectivity, which targets may construct a validated Glucose Reading, or what happens to a Team-ID-templated container when a Builder changes team or recreates their fork (which under fork-and-build they will). This is the structural replacement for the Wear Data Layer and is neither an FR nor a recorded loss (research coverage gap 6). NFR-19's 'no health value is written outside that store: not to an App Group plist' partially contradicts FR-116's shared cache.

BGM SOURCE CAPABILITY HAS NO CONSUMING SURFACE. FR-24 and FR-30 declare BGM source as a multi-instance Capability and FR-24 says two concurrent BGM sources 'produce readings distinguished by the meter name on the reading'. No FR in 5.3, 5.5 or 5.8 renders a BGM reading, stores it, reconciles it with a CGM Glucose Reading, or says whether it participates in Time in Range, the Alert Floor or the Watch relay. A declared Capability with no downstream requirement.

CALIBRATION HAS NO USER FLOW. Calibration target is one of the seven Capabilities (FR-30), FR-31 classifies `calibrate` as a permitted device-touching operation, FR-234 publishes it, and FR-30 resolves a 'calibration slot'. No FR specifies a calibration surface, its input validation against the Glucose Validity Bound, or its gating by Verification Status. Either it is a shipped feature with no requirement or a reserved slot that should be declared as such (see the SI-1 contradiction).

TROUBLESHOOTING AND STATUS-ICON DOCUMENTATION PAGES ARE THE NAMED DISCLOSURE SURFACE FOR FIVE FORCED LOSSES AND ARE REQUIRED BY NO FR. PL-1 (bond removal), PL-2 (stale service cache), PL-8 (unstable pairing identity), PL-10 (Bluetooth glyph) and PL-52 (battery-optimization) all cite 'the pairing-troubleshooting page' or 'the iOS status-icons page'. 5.12 has FRs for the directory contract (FR-219), basenames (FR-220), the install runbook (FR-223), the Watch setup page (FR-224) and contributor docs (FR-225) — and nothing that requires a troubleshooting page to exist or to carry those statements. §7.5 itself says 'a forced loss with no disclosure surface is a defect'.

PARITY LEDGER ROWS PROMISED BY §6 AND NEVER WRITTEN. Four NFRs explicitly say 'Recorded in the Parity Ledger' for divergences that appear in no PL/PD/PA row: NFR-15 (Android's `fallbackToDestructiveMigration()` deliberately not reproduced — verified absent from §7); NFR-7 (the 30-day chart's oldest-end truncation at 2,000 rows 'stated in the Parity Ledger as inherited Android behaviour'); NFR-31 ('Parity Ledger entry: matched' for localization); NFR-32/NFR-33 (the project can never receive a crash report or a device log, and the in-app log buffer has honest gaps where Android's foreground service produced a continuous process-level record). PA-15 records the export, not the loss.

NO PD ROW FOR THE PUMP-IDENTITY DISPLAY FIX. FR-19 corrects a real Android defect — the raw MAC address was rendered unmasked as the Pump subtitle in the pairing screen and the Settings card — and the section's own notes ask for it. PL-8 covers only address-as-stable-pairing-key. The user-visible display change has no PD row, and PL-8's own [NOTE FOR PM] flags that FR-19 never states the reinstall/restore consequence to the user either.

ONBOARDING PROMISES A FEATURE THAT SHIPS NOWHERE. FR-159's Features card copy is fixed verbatim as 'With a connected server, get daily briefs, meal analysis, and pattern recognition…', and FR-170 labels a sound row 'AI analysis insights and daily briefs'. 5.6's Out of Scope states the app ships no brief surface, no brief view model and no brief endpoint call, and that the absence is 'preserved deliberately'. 5.6's own note flags that the Android copy inconsistency 'ports along with the copy unless 5.9 fixes the onboarding wording' — 5.9 did not fix it, and there is no ledger row.

DEEP LINKS AND WIDGET/COMPLICATION ENTRY POINTS ARE ADDITIVE SCOPE WITH NO PA ROW. Research verified Android registers no deep links, no `ACTION_VIEW` intent filters, no AppWidgetProvider, no TileService and no ShortcutManager, and warned that every iOS widget, Lock Screen widget, Smart Stack entry and complication 'must be framed as additive scope, not parity restoration'. PA-2 and PA-3 do this for widgets and complications; the deep-link surface required by FR-63, FR-105 and FR-114 (including a 500-character prefill payload) has no PA row and directly conflicts with NFR-22.
safety_invariant_coverage: SI-1 (no therapeutic write) — COVERED, 21 FRs name it: FR-2, FR-8, FR-12, FR-13, FR-21, FR-30, FR-31, FR-71, FR-90, FR-96, FR-111, FR-113, FR-114, FR-115, FR-160, FR-189, FR-205, FR-225, FR-226, FR-234, plus NFR-21 and NG-1. Load-bearing owners: FR-31 (read-only by construction) and FR-205 (API-surface snapshot gate). CAVEAT — this is the one invariant whose coverage is contradicted rather than absent: FR-30/FR-31/FR-234 all classify `calibrate` as a permitted device-touching operation while SI-1 forbids 'any device command', and FR-205's gate would fail the protocol that declares it. Not orphaned; unresolved.

SI-2 (reject never clamp, never precondition) — COVERED, 26 FRs: FR-28, FR-32, FR-35, FR-36, FR-49, FR-58, FR-64, FR-79, FR-81, FR-92, FR-100, FR-116, FR-120, FR-125, FR-133, FR-138, FR-146, FR-155, FR-169, FR-172, FR-178, FR-206, FR-217, FR-225, FR-226, FR-234, plus NFR-14. The 'never `precondition`' half is explicitly carried by FR-28, FR-49, FR-90, FR-138, FR-206, FR-217 Layer 2 and NFR-14, and is enforced by a named SwiftLint rule in FR-208. Strongest-covered invariant in the document.

SI-3 (mg/dL canonical, mmol/L display-only) — COVERED, 19 FRs: FR-32, FR-46, FR-47, FR-52, FR-59, FR-60, FR-69, FR-79, FR-92, FR-116, FR-120, FR-124, FR-133, FR-138, FR-158, FR-169, FR-172, FR-175, FR-217. FR-47 and FR-124 both make it structural ('the colour/banding function accepts no unit parameter'), which is the strongest form available.

SI-4 (one definition per Safety Constant, linked by phone and Watch) — COVERED, 11 FRs: FR-32, FR-49, FR-60, FR-72, FR-88, FR-92, FR-116, FR-138, FR-175, FR-210, FR-217, plus NFR-4. FR-217's inverse scan is the mechanism. WEAKNESS — three sections restate the pinned mmol/L conversion fixture (FR-60, FR-116, FR-175) and FR-116's copy is incomplete, which is precisely the drift SI-4 exists to prevent.

SI-5 (Alert Floor never fires from stale data or unconfirmed thresholds) — COVERED, 28 FRs: FR-34, FR-49, FR-64, FR-71, FR-72, FR-73, FR-74, FR-75, FR-81, FR-82, FR-86, FR-123, FR-125, FR-128, FR-129, FR-130, FR-143, FR-144, FR-149, FR-164, FR-165, FR-167, FR-168, FR-169, FR-176, FR-234, FR-235, plus NFR-12. FR-73 is the dedicated provenance owner and FR-72 the dedicated freshness owner; both are properly gated and pinned by boundary pairs.

SI-6 (Coverage Claim never overstates) — COVERED, 49 FRs — the most widely referenced invariant. Dedicated owners: FR-83 (one selector), FR-84 (expiry and decay), FR-85 (proactive lapse notification), FR-126 (wrist renders and decays, never derives). The 'Watch never derives its own claim' clause is explicitly upheld in FR-84, FR-126 and FR-172.

SI-7 (only completed deliveries; SmartGuard micro-boluses excluded) — COVERED, 11 FRs: FR-53, FR-89, FR-90, FR-91, FR-121, FR-132, FR-137, FR-140, FR-153, FR-206, FR-226. FR-90 is the dedicated owner. The SmartGuard exclusion is stated in FR-90 (at Driver decode time, per A-13), FR-132 and FR-140.

SI-8 (cursors never advance past an undecoded record) — COVERED but THINNEST, only 6 FRs: FR-36, FR-40, FR-132, FR-146, FR-206, FR-226, plus NFR-9 and NFR-13. Substantive owners are FR-146 (resumable history download) and FR-206 (replay test asserting non-advance). NOTE: FR-40's 'Upholds SI-8' tag is spurious — pull-to-refresh touches no history cursor — so the effective FR count is five. Given R-9 rates cursor loss as a High risk and both Android cursors are process-local today, SI-8 deserves a dedicated FR in 5.2 stating the cursor durability contract at the Driver-protocol level rather than only per-consumer.

SI-9 (no health value, payload or credential at or above debug level) — COVERED, 25 FRs: FR-19, FR-35, FR-42, FR-81, FR-88, FR-90, FR-95, FR-104, FR-108, FR-109, FR-114, FR-134, FR-135, FR-139, FR-153, FR-158, FR-176, FR-180, FR-185, FR-189, FR-200, FR-204, FR-221, FR-226, FR-236, plus NFR-24. NFR-24 adds the iOS-specific unified-logging trap (numeric interpolations are public by default) that no FR states — that belongs in FR-158.

SI-10 (Keychain, device-only, after-first-unlock) — COVERED, 15 FRs: FR-14, FR-18, FR-29, FR-75, FR-88, FR-135, FR-136, FR-161, FR-167, FR-169, FR-181, FR-182, FR-204, FR-226, FR-236, plus NFR-18. All agree on `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` and FR-204 makes any other class a build failure. The only inconsistency is that §15 OQ-1 still lists the class as blocking-unresolved.

SI-11 (Backend Safety Limits may only narrow) — COVERED, 10 FRs: FR-32, FR-42, FR-58, FR-80, FR-125, FR-138, FR-155, FR-168, FR-214, FR-216. FR-32 is the dedicated owner with the full clamp ordering. WEAKNESS: FR-153 validates Nightscout-sourced rows against the absolute Bound rather than the narrowed Safety Limits, so SI-11's narrowing does not reach one ingest path (see contradictions).

SI-12 (unknown fields tolerated, missing consumed field fails loudly) — COVERED, 9 FRs: FR-65, FR-98, FR-102, FR-104, FR-111, FR-114, FR-155, FR-214, FR-215. FR-215 is the dedicated owner and explicitly names the Swift synthesized-`Codable` failure mode the invariant calls out. One recorded carve-out (FR-98 / A-16, the two dispersion flags) is requested against SI-12 and is still awaiting a ruling (§15 OQ-36 / R-8).

NO ORPHANED INVARIANT. All twelve are named by at least one FR and each has an identifiable dedicated owner. The two weakest are SI-8 (five substantive FRs, no Driver-protocol-level cursor durability requirement) and SI-1 (widely covered but actively contradicted by the calibration Capability).
